summary: Bind the canonical public export identity to a content digest of the Node export worker bundle so a worker code fix produces a new identity while identical code keeps cache reuse.
invariants: exporter_digest is a sha256 over the on-disk sources the isolated hybrid export worker executes: the assembler entrypoint, servers/nextjs/scripts/lib non-test .mjs helpers, servers/nextjs/lib/presentation-export-quality.ts, and non-test sources under servers/nextjs/lib/authored-hybrid.
The worker protocol string stays exporter_version and is folded into the digest payload, so a protocol bump also splits the identity.
The digest is computed once per process from file bytes and recorded relative to the Next.js root, so two checkouts of identical code share one identity.
An unreadable or incomplete worker tree falls back to a stable digest over the protocol string plus the 'bundle-unavailable' marker, and the operation receipt records source and reason.
The receipt key exporterWorkerBundle names the worker code that produced the delivered bytes.
forbidden: Derive exporter_digest from the protocol string alone: a completed identity is reused unconditionally, so a broken worker would be served from cache forever.
Include test files, spec files, or fixtures in the bundle inventory: they never execute in the worker and would invalidate published exports on a test-only edit.
Add a manual cache-invalidation switch in place of the content binding.
